summary: Master Earned Value Management with practical EVM calculations, forecasting, and reporting. Learn to control cost and schedule with confidence.
lede: Earned value management combines project scope, schedule, and cost data to assess performance against a plan. For project managers, project controls analysts, planning and cost engineers, and others working with plans, budgets, or progress updates, it covers control accounts and baselines, collecting planned value, earned value, and actual cost, and calculating variances and forecasts. Learners also interpret performance trends and prepare reports and dashboards to support corrective action.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with project plans, budgets, and progress updates and now need to apply Earned Value Management with confidence. It is suitable for people who touch the data, review the reports, or lead the corrective actions that follow from the numbers. Project Controls Analyst responsible for earned value data quality and reporting. Project Manager accountable for project cost and schedule performance. Planning Engineer maintaining baseline schedules and progress measurement logic. Cost Engineer tracking actual cost, variance, and forecast behaviour. Control Account Manager managing control accounts and corrective actions. Project Scheduler updating logic, milestones, and performance baselines. Project Cost Controller reconciling costs and supporting monthly reviews. PMO Analyst standardizing project status metrics and dashboards. Program Controls Lead consolidating earned value views across projects. Contract Administrator monitoring baseline changes and reporting implications.
prerequisites: You should bring a calculator and a laptop with Microsoft Excel or an equivalent spreadsheet tool. Prior exposure to project scheduling concepts, baseline budgets, and progress reporting will help you move faster through the calculations and analysis exercises.
